sources.title: First and Second Stage Labor Management | ACOG

reply.text: Childbirth varies a lot, and the timing depends on the stage of labour. NICE says the established first stage starts with regular contractions and dilation from 4 cm; first labours average about 8 hours and are unlikely to last over 18 hours, while later labours average about 5 hours and are unlikely to last over 12 hours [1]. ACOG separates labour into first, second and third stages [2].

sources.title: How to Tell When Labor Begins | ACOG
Duration of spontaneous labour in ‘low-risk’ women with ‘normal’ perinatal outcomes: A systematic review - PMC

reply.text: Yes — for a second or later labour, the first stage is usually shorter. NICE says the established first stage averages about 5 hours and is unlikely to last over 12 hours, compared with about 8 hours and up to 18 hours for a first labour [1]. ACOG gives a broader whole-labour estimate of 8–10 hours if you’ve given birth before, versus 12–18 hours for a first baby [2].
